qns_content.text: Which layer in the dicot root prevents water loss and has casparian strips?

text_solutions: The endodermis contains Casparian strips that prevent the passive movement of water, regulating transport into the vascular tissue.

qns_content.text: What differentiates an isobilateral leaf from a dorsiventral leaf?

text_solutions: Isobilateral leaves (e.g., monocots) have stomata on both surfaces, whereas dorsiventral leaves (e.g., dicots) have stomata mostly on the lower surface.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about stomatal apparatus is correct?

options.text: Stomatal pores are surrounded by specialized guard cells.
Subsidiary cells are always absent in the stomatal complex.
Stomata are present only in stems and absent in leaves.

text_solutions: Stomata are surrounded by specialized guard cells, which regulate the opening and closing of the stomatal pore.

qns_content.text: Which type of simple permanent tissue provides mechanical support in mature plants?

text_solutions: Sclerenchyma consists of thick-walled, lignified cells that provide mechanical support in mature plants.

qns_content.text: In monocot stems, the vascular bundles are surrounded by which type of supportive tissue?

text_solutions: In monocot stems, each vascular bundle is surrounded by a sheath of sclerenchyma, which provides mechanical support.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the hypodermis in monocot stems is incorrect?

options.text: It is present just below the epidermis.

text_solutions: The hypodermis in monocot stems is made of sclerenchyma, whereas in dicot stems, it is made of collenchyma.

qns_content.text: What is the function of bulliform cells in monocot leaves?

text_solutions: Bulliform cells help in folding the leaves to reduce water loss under drought conditions.

qns_content.text: Which of the following plant tissues is responsible for the transport of food?

text_solutions: Phloem is responsible for transporting organic nutrients, primarily sucrose, from source to sink in plants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about collenchyma is incorrect?

options.text: Collenchyma provides mechanical support to young stems and leaves.
Collenchyma cells have unevenly thickened cell walls.
Collenchyma contains pectin and cellulose in its cell walls.

text_solutions: Collenchyma cells remain living at maturity and provide flexibility and mechanical support to growing plant parts.

qns_content.text: Which characteristic feature of dicot roots helps in selective absorption of water?

text_solutions: The endodermis in dicot roots contains Casparian strips, which regulate selective water absorption into the vascular bundle.

qns_content.text: Which layer of cells in a dicot root lies just inside the endodermis?

text_solutions: The pericycle is the layer of cells located just inside the endodermis and is responsible for the initiation of lateral roots.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about epidermis in plants is incorrect?

options.text: The epidermis is usually a single layer of cells.
The epidermis helps in reducing water loss.
Trichomes are part of the epidermal tissue system.

text_solutions: Epidermal cells generally lack chloroplasts, except for guard cells, which regulate stomatal opening.

qns_content.text: Which cells in the vascular bundle provide structural support?

text_solutions: Sclerenchyma fibers in vascular bundles provide mechanical strength and support to plants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about xylem parenchyma is correct?

options.text: Xylem parenchyma stores food and helps in lateral conduction of water.
Xylem parenchyma is responsible for the conduction of water.
Xylem parenchyma is composed of lignified dead cells.

text_solutions: Xylem parenchyma consists of living cells that store starch and fats and assist in lateral water conduction.

qns_content.text: Which type of plant cells provide flexibility to young stems and leaves?

text_solutions: Collenchyma cells provide flexibility and mechanical support to young stems and leaves.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about sieve tube elements in phloem is correct?

options.text: Sieve tube elements have nuclei at maturity.
Sieve tube elements are supported by companion cells.
Sieve tube elements are responsible for water transport.
Sieve tube elements have thick, lignified walls.

text_solutions: Sieve tube elements lack nuclei and depend on companion cells for their function in transporting food.

qns_content.text: What is the function of the casparian strip in the endodermis of roots?

text_solutions: The casparian strip prevents passive movement of water and minerals, forcing selective absorption through plasma membranes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about root hairs is correct?

options.text: Root hairs increase the surface area for absorption of water and minerals.
Root hairs are responsible for the transport of organic nutrients.

text_solutions: Root hairs are extensions of epidermal cells that increase the surface area for absorption of water and minerals.

qns_content.text: What is the function of guard cells in stomata?

text_solutions: Guard cells regulate the opening and closing of stomatal pores to control transpiration and gas exchange.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about bundle sheath cells is incorrect?

options.text: Bundle sheath cells regulate the movement of substances into and out of vascular tissues.
Bundle sheath cells are present only in monocots.

text_solutions: Bundle sheath cells are present in both monocots and dicots, although they are more specialized in C4 plants.

qns_content.text: Which simple tissue in plants is responsible for photosynthesis in leaves?

text_solutions: Parenchyma in leaves contains chloroplasts and is called mesophyll, which carries out photosynthesis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about sclerenchyma is incorrect?

text_solutions: Sclerenchyma cells have thick, lignified walls that provide strength and rigidity to plant structures.

qns_content.text: What is the main function of phloem in vascular plants?

text_solutions: Phloem transports organic nutrients like sucrose from the leaves to other parts of the plant.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about casparian strips in endodermis is incorrect?

options.text: Casparian strips regulate water movement into the vascular bundle.
Casparian strips are made up of suberin.

text_solutions: Casparian strips are found in the endodermis, not in phloem, and they regulate the entry of water and solutes into vascular tissue.

qns_content.text: What is the main function of trichomes in the shoot system?

text_solutions: Trichomes reduce water loss by minimizing transpiration and can also provide protection.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about xylem vessels is incorrect?

options.text: Xylem vessels help in the transport of water and minerals.

text_solutions: Xylem vessels are dead at maturity and function in conducting water and minerals from roots to other plant parts.

qns_content.text: Which part of the root stores starch and other nutrients?

text_solutions: The cortex of roots is responsible for storing starch and other nutrients.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about intercalary meristem is incorrect?

options.text: Intercalary meristem is found in grasses and bamboo.
Intercalary meristem helps in elongation of internodes.
Intercalary meristem is located at the tip of the root and shoot.
Intercalary meristem is a type of primary meristem.

text_solutions: Intercalary meristem is located at the base of leaves and internodes, not at the tips of roots and shoots.

qns_content.text: What is the primary function of the pericycle in dicot roots?

text_solutions: The pericycle in dicot roots plays a crucial role in the initiation of lateral roots and secondary growth.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about phloem loading is incorrect?

options.text: Phloem loading refers to the movement of sucrose into sieve tube elements.
Phloem loading occurs actively through companion cells.
Phloem loading occurs primarily through xylem vessels.

text_solutions: Phloem loading occurs via sieve tube elements and companion cells, not through xylem vessels.

qns_content.text: Which vascular tissue transports food in plants?

text_solutions: Phloem is responsible for the transport of organic nutrients, particularly sucrose, from the leaves to different parts of the plant.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about sclerenchyma is correct?

options.text: Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and provide mechanical support.
Sclerenchyma has thin primary walls with intercellular spaces.

text_solutions: Sclerenchyma consists of dead cells with thick lignified walls, providing mechanical support to the plant.

qns_content.text: Which part of a dicot stem contains the starch sheath?

text_solutions: In dicot stems, the endodermis is rich in starch grains and is known as the starch sheath.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the endodermis in dicot roots is correct?

options.text: It is the outermost layer of the root.
It consists of loosely arranged cells with intercellular spaces.
It contains Casparian strips, which regulate water movement.
It is made up of dead cells.

text_solutions: The endodermis has Casparian strips, which prevent passive water flow and regulate selective absorption.

qns_content.text: Which cells are responsible for opening and closing of stomata?

text_solutions: Guard cells control the opening and closing of stomata by regulating turgor pressure.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about trichomes is correct?

options.text: Trichomes are found on roots and help in absorption.
Trichomes help in reducing water loss from aerial parts.
Trichomes are present in xylem and help in conduction.
Trichomes are involved in transport of organic nutrients.

text_solutions: Trichomes are epidermal outgrowths that help in reducing transpiration and protecting the plant from herbivores.

qns_content.text: Which type of vascular bundle is found in monocot roots?

text_solutions: Monocot roots have radial, polyarch vascular bundles, meaning they have multiple xylem bundles arranged radially.

qns_content.text: Which type of simple permanent tissue stores food and is involved in photosynthesis?

text_solutions: Parenchyma is responsible for food storage and, when containing chloroplasts, participates in photosynthesis.

qns_content.text: Which type of plant tissue is present in the pericycle and contributes to lateral root formation?

text_solutions: Parenchyma in the pericycle contributes to the formation of lateral roots in dicot plants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the cortex in roots is correct?

options.text: The cortex is composed of lignified dead cells.
The cortex helps in water and nutrient storage.
The cortex is the innermost layer of the root.

text_solutions: The cortex consists of parenchymatous cells and stores water, nutrients, and starch in roots.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the main function of the epidermis in plants?

text_solutions: The epidermis forms the outermost protective layer of the plant body and prevents excessive water loss.

qns_content.text: What is the function of bundle sheath cells in vascular bundles?

text_solutions: Bundle sheath cells in vascular bundles provide mechanical support to vascular tissues.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the epidermis in plants is correct?

options.text: The epidermis is a single layer of cells that provides protection.
The epidermis consists of loosely packed cells with large intercellular spaces.
The epidermis is mainly responsible for transport of water and nutrients.

text_solutions: The epidermis is a protective layer made of closely packed cells, which reduces water loss and protects internal tissues.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about xylem is incorrect?

options.text: Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to shoots.
Tracheids and vessels are the conducting elements of xylem.
Xylem is a complex tissue composed of different cell types.

text_solutions: Xylem fibers provide mechanical support, while conduction of water is performed by tracheids and vessels.

qns_content.text: What is the primary function of the endodermis in roots?

text_solutions: The endodermis has Casparian strips, which regulate the movement of water and minerals into the vascular tissue.

qns_content.text: Which plant tissue is responsible for the transport of water and minerals?

text_solutions: Xylem is responsible for the transport of water and minerals from the roots to other parts of the plant.

qns_content.text: Which tissue system includes the epidermis, stomata, and trichomes?

text_solutions: The epidermal tissue system consists of the epidermis, stomata, and trichomes, which provide protection and regulate gas exchange.

qns_content.text: Which of the following tissues provides mechanical support and flexibility?

text_solutions: Collenchyma provides mechanical support while allowing flexibility in young stems and leaves.

qns_content.text: Which type of vascular bundle arrangement is present in roots?

text_solutions: In roots, vascular bundles are radial, where xylem and phloem are arranged on different radii.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about dicot leaves is incorrect?

options.text: Dicot leaves have differentiated palisade and spongy mesophyll.
Vascular bundles in dicot leaves are arranged in a branching pattern.

text_solutions: Dicot leaves have stomata, primarily on the lower epidermis, for gas exchange and transpiration.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about stomata is correct?

options.text: Each stoma is surrounded by guard cells.
Stomata are absent in leaves and present only in stems.
The outer walls of guard cells are thick, and the inner walls are thin.

text_solutions: Each stoma is surrounded by two guard cells, which regulate its opening and closing. The outer walls are thin, and the inner walls are thick.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about phloem is incorrect?

options.text: Phloem transports food from source to sink.
Sieve tube elements have companion cells to support their function.

text_solutions: Phloem does not contain xylem vessels; instead, it consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibers, and phloem parenchyma.

qns_content.text: Which type of simple permanent tissue makes up the majority of the cortex in dicot roots?

text_solutions: The cortex of dicot roots consists mostly of parenchymatous cells, which store food and provide structural support.

qns_content.text: Which type of plant tissue consists of actively dividing cells?

text_solutions: Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing cells that contribute to plant growth.

qns_content.text: Which structure in dicot stems lies between the vascular bundles and helps in lateral conduction?

text_solutions: Medullary rays in dicot stems are parenchymatous cells that facilitate lateral conduction of nutrients and water.

qns_content.text: Which layer of the dicot stem is rich in starch grains and is also called the starch sheath?

text_solutions: In dicot stems, the endodermis is rich in starch grains and is referred to as the starch sheath.

qns_content.text: Which characteristic differentiates monocot stems from dicot stems?

text_solutions: Monocot stems have vascular bundles scattered throughout the ground tissue, unlike dicot stems, which have a ring arrangement.

qns_content.text: Which layer of the root is directly responsible for the absorption of water and minerals?

text_solutions: The epidermis, especially its root hairs, absorbs water and minerals from the soil.

qns_content.text: What type of vascular bundle is found in leaves?

text_solutions: Leaves have conjoint vascular bundles where xylem and phloem are together on the same radius.

qns_content.text: Which type of mesophyll tissue is responsible for maximum photosynthesis in dicot leaves?

text_solutions: Palisade parenchyma cells contain abundant chloroplasts and carry out most of the photosynthesis in dicot leaves.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the epidermal tissue system is correct?

options.text: The epidermis is usually single-layered and protects the plant.
Epidermal cells are dead at maturity and have thick walls.
Stomata are present in roots for gaseous exchange.
The cuticle is present in all plant organs, including roots.

text_solutions: The epidermis is a single-layered protective layer in plants. It is made up of living cells, and the cuticle is absent in roots.

qns_content.text: Which part of the dicot stem lies between the vascular bundles and functions in lateral conduction?

text_solutions: Medullary rays are parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles that aid in lateral conduction.

qns_content.text: Which cells in the leaves help in minimizing water loss by curling under dry conditions?

text_solutions: Bulliform cells help in minimizing water loss by causing the leaf to curl inward under water stress conditions.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about companion cells in phloem is correct?

options.text: Companion cells help in the functioning of sieve tube elements.

text_solutions: Companion cells are living cells that help regulate the function of sieve tube elements in transporting organic nutrients.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about bulliform cells in monocot leaves is correct?

options.text: They help in leaf rolling under drought conditions.

text_solutions: Bulliform cells help in leaf rolling during water stress, reducing water loss in monocot leaves.

qns_content.text: Which cells are responsible for giving strength to vascular bundles in monocot stems?

text_solutions: In monocot stems, each vascular bundle is surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, which provides strength and support.

qns_content.text: Which type of ground tissue is responsible for providing mechanical support in young stems?

text_solutions: Collenchyma provides mechanical support to young growing stems and petioles.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about monocot leaves is incorrect?

options.text: Bulliform cells help in leaf rolling during water stress.
Mesophyll in monocot leaves is differentiated into palisade and spongy layers.
Monocot leaves have stomata on both surfaces.

text_solutions: In monocot leaves, mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma, unlike dicot leaves.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about mesophyll in leaves is correct?

options.text: Mesophyll is made up of xylem and phloem tissues.

text_solutions: Mesophyll contains chloroplasts and is responsible for photosynthesis in leaves.

qns_content.text: Which plant tissue is responsible for the transport of organic nutrients?

text_solutions: Phloem is responsible for the transport of organic nutrients, mainly sucrose, from source to sink in plants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about dicot and monocot leaves is correct?

options.text: Dicot leaves have palisade and spongy mesophyll
Monocot leaves have a ring of vascular bundles

text_solutions: Dicot leaves have distinct palisade and spongy mesophyll layers, while monocot leaves do not show this differentiation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the ground tissue system is incorrect?

options.text: It includes all tissues except epidermis and vascular tissues.
It is mainly composed of parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma.
Mesophyll in leaves is a part of the ground tissue system.

text_solutions: The ground tissue system includes mesophyll, which contains chloroplasts and plays an essential role in photosynthesis.

qns_content.text: Which part of a plant is composed mainly of simple tissues?

text_solutions: The ground tissue consists mostly of simple tissues like parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about pericycle in roots is correct?

options.text: The pericycle is the innermost layer of the cortex.
The pericycle gives rise to lateral roots.
The pericycle is absent in dicot roots.
The pericycle is made up of xylem and phloem tissues.

text_solutions: The pericycle is responsible for the initiation of lateral roots in dicot and monocot roots.

qns_content.text: Which layer in dicot roots lies between the epidermis and the vascular bundle?

text_solutions: The cortex lies between the epidermis and vascular bundle and consists mainly of parenchymatous cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about endodermis in roots is correct?

options.text: Endodermis is the outermost layer of the root.
Endodermis is made up of dead cells.

text_solutions: Endodermis cells contain Casparian strips, which help regulate the movement of water and solutes into the vascular bundle.

qns_content.text: Which of the following structures is unique to monocot leaves?

text_solutions: Bulliform cells in monocot leaves help in minimizing water loss by curling the leaves under drought conditions.

qns_content.text: Which vascular tissue component provides structural support in plants?

text_solutions: Tracheids are elongated, lignified cells in xylem that provide structural support and facilitate water conduction.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of isobilateral (monocot) leaves?

options.text: Stomata are present only on the lower epidermis
Mesophyll is differentiated into palisade and spongy layers
Bulliform cells help in rolling the leaves

text_solutions: Bulliform cells in monocot leaves help in rolling the leaves during water stress to minimize water loss.

qns_content.text: Which cells form the majority of the mesophyll in monocot leaves?

text_solutions: In monocot leaves, the mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma as in dicots.

qns_content.text: Which of the following cells in the epidermis help in the regulation of stomatal movement?

text_solutions: Guard cells surround the stomatal pore and regulate its opening and closing.

qns_content.text: Which cells in leaves are responsible for photosynthesis?

text_solutions: Mesophyll cells, consisting of palisade and spongy parenchyma, contain chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis.

qns_content.text: Which structure in dicot roots stores food?

text_solutions: The cortex of dicot roots consists of parenchymatous cells that store food and nutrients.

qns_content.text: Which component of xylem is responsible for the conduction of water?

text_solutions: Tracheids are elongated cells in xylem responsible for conducting water in vascular plants.

qns_content.text: Which layer of cells in the root prevents the passive flow of water and minerals into the vascular bundle?

text_solutions: The endodermis contains Casparian strips, which regulate the movement of water and minerals into the vascular bundle.

qns_content.text: Which vascular tissue in plants lacks nuclei?

text_solutions: Sieve tube elements in phloem lack nuclei and rely on companion cells for their functions.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about lateral roots is correct?

text_solutions: Lateral roots arise from the pericycle, making them endogenous in origin.

qns_content.text: Which type of vascular bundle is commonly found in roots?

text_solutions: Radial vascular bundles are found in roots, where xylem and phloem are arranged separately along different radii.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the epidermis of plants is true?

options.text: It is made up of loosely packed cells
It usually contains a cuticle to prevent water loss

text_solutions: The epidermis is usually covered by a waxy cuticle to prevent excessive water loss.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of dicot stems?

text_solutions: Dicot stems have vascular bundles arranged in a ring, whereas monocot stems have scattered vascular bundles.

qns_content.text: What is the function of root hairs?

text_solutions: Root hairs increase the surface area of roots for better absorption of water and minerals from the soil.

qns_content.text: Which cells in plants regulate transpiration?

text_solutions: Guard cells regulate the opening and closing of stomata, thereby controlling transpiration in plants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about phloem is correct?

options.text: Phloem transports organic nutrients from leaves to other parts of the plant.
Sieve tube elements have nuclei and are independent cells.
Phloem consists only of parenchyma and sclerenchyma.
Phloem fibers are the main conducting elements.

text_solutions: Phloem transports organic nutrients such as sucrose. Sieve tube elements lack nuclei and function with the help of companion cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about phloem fibers is incorrect?

options.text: Phloem fibers are the only dead component of phloem.
Phloem fibers are also called bast fibers.

text_solutions: Phloem fibers are usually dead at maturity and provide mechanical strength to the plant.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about monocot leaves is correct?

options.text: Bulliform cells help in minimizing water loss.
Monocot leaves have mesophyll differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma.

text_solutions: Bulliform cells help in rolling the leaves under dry conditions, reducing water loss.

qns_content.text: Which tissue system in plants is responsible for the transportation of water and nutrients?

text_solutions: The vascular tissue system, consisting of xylem and phloem, is responsible for the conduction of water, nutrients, and food in plants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of the epidermal tissue system?

text_solutions: Xylem is a part of the vascular tissue system, whereas stomata, trichomes, and epidermal cells belong to the epidermal tissue system.

qns_content.text: Which characteristic feature is present in dicot leaves but absent in monocot leaves?

text_solutions: Dicot leaves have palisade and spongy mesophyll, which are not distinctly differentiated in monocot leaves.

qns_content.text: Which cells in the root actively regulate the movement of water and minerals into the vascular tissue?

text_solutions: Endodermal cells contain Casparian strips, which regulate the selective movement of water and minerals into the vascular tissue.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the xylem is incorrect?

options.text: Xylem parenchyma stores food and conducts water laterally.

text_solutions: Xylem vessels are dead at maturity and function in water transport.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about medullary rays in dicot stems is correct?

options.text: Medullary rays are made of parenchyma and help in lateral conduction.
Medullary rays are absent in dicot stems.
Medullary rays are made of sclerenchyma and provide mechanical strength.
Medullary rays are found only in monocot stems.

text_solutions: Medullary rays are parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles that facilitate lateral conduction in dicot stems.

qns_content.text: Which of the following tissues is responsible for providing flexibility to plant stems?

text_solutions: Collenchyma provides mechanical support while allowing flexibility in young stems and petioles.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about xylem and phloem is correct?

options.text: Xylem transports food, while phloem transports water
Xylem conducts water, while phloem conducts organic nutrients
Phloem conducts water, while xylem conducts organic nutrients

text_solutions: Xylem transports water and minerals, while phloem transports organic nutrients such as sucrose.

qns_content.text: Which tissue in the vascular system is responsible for the transport of water and minerals?

text_solutions: Xylem is responsible for transporting water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.

qns_content.text: In which type of plants are vascular bundles found scattered throughout the ground tissue?

text_solutions: In monocot stems, vascular bundles are scattered within the ground tissue and lack cambium.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about medullary rays in dicot stems is incorrect?

options.text: They are responsible for lateral conduction of nutrients.

text_solutions: Medullary rays are present in dicot stems and play a role in lateral conduction of nutrients.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about pith in monocot roots is correct?

options.text: Pith in monocot roots is composed of sclerenchyma.
Pith in monocot roots functions in photosynthesis.

text_solutions: Monocot roots have a well-developed pith, whereas in dicot roots, the pith is either small or absent.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about tracheids is correct?

options.text: Tracheids are living cells involved in conduction.
Tracheids have perforation plates for efficient conduction.
Tracheids provide both mechanical support and water conduction.

text_solutions: Tracheids are dead cells with thick lignified walls that help in both mechanical support and water conduction.

qns_content.text: Which part of the dicot leaf contains chloroplasts and is responsible for photosynthesis?

text_solutions: Mesophyll consists of palisade and spongy parenchyma, both of which contain chloroplasts and perform photosynthesis.

qns_content.text: In which type of vascular bundle are xylem and phloem arranged in an alternate manner along different radii?

text_solutions: In radial vascular bundles, xylem and phloem are arranged alternately, as seen in roots.
